lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: This is the Harbour, on one hundred and forty point oh. The light's on. Come in slow.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: The Harbour. Rest for relay ships, and for whoever's sitting in the chair.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Kettle's on.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: You've found the Harbour. Well. You were brought. Same thing, in the end.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: The Harbour, at the end of the long drift. Berth seven is yours. It always has been.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: The Harbourmaster's office. Lights on the piers, and a radio for anyone coming in.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Evening Berths, from the Harbour.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Ships coming in out of the dark, one at a time. I'll talk you in.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Lights on the Water. Everyone's moored. Everyone's quiet.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Just me, the kettle, and whoever's still awake.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: The Morning Tide. Lines off at first light.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: They always go in the morning.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Evening, Nightjar. Evening, operator. I'm the Harbourmaster.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: You'll be tired. Everyone's tired when they get here. Berth seven, on your left, with the light on.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Take it slow. There's no hurry. There never was.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Evening, HUSH.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: Evening, Harbourmaster.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Hull's a bit dusty.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: We came the long way.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: You always do.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: I've brought the operator.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: So I see. Hello, operator. She's told me all about you.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: I haven't said a word.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: No. You never do.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Relay ships drift a long way between harbours. Years, some of them. Nobody's meant to drift forever. Not even a ship.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: So they come here, for a night. Tie up. Turn the instruments down. Let somebody else keep watch for once.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Then they go back out. That's all this is. A night off.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: She didn't tell you where you were going, did she. No. They never do.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: It isn't secrecy. Say a place out loud too early, and you start to worry it won't be there.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: It's always here.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Last time the Nightjar came in, the operator before you brought a bag of oranges. We sat out on the pier and peeled them.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: She said HUSH hummed all the way here. Through the air vents. I believe her.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Relay Four was in, last spring. Teodor slept for fourteen hours.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: When he woke up, he didn't ask whether anyone was receiving. Not once. He just had his breakfast. Nicest thing I've ever seen.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Kettle's on. There's a mug for you on the hook. Every operator gets one.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Yours has a little star on it. I painted it this morning. I knew you were coming.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: I keep a log too. Not like hers. Mine only says who came in, and whether they slept.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Tonight it says, Nightjar, and her operator. Write the rest in yourself, if you like. In your writing.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: On a clear night you can see the Last Lighthouse from the end of the long pier. Very small.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: The Keeper and I wave. Neither of us has ever seen the other wave back. We both keep doing it.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Lights coming up out of the dark. That'll be Relay Two, and behind her, a little survey ship that's never been in before.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: First time's always slow. They don't believe the light's for them. It is. Come on in.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Berth seven, you're tied up. Well done. Leave the engines. Leave the heading. Nobody needs a heading in a harbour.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Put your feet up. That's an order. The only one I give.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Three old relays asleep along the long pier tonight. Relay Two, Relay Eleven, and one so old she hasn't got a number, only a name.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Ships snore, you know. Very softly. A sort of hum.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Your ship's asleep. First time in a long time. I can tell, because her heading light's gone out.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Don't wake her. She's earned it. I'll keep the watch tonight. That's what I'm for.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Tide's turning. Ships leave in the morning. They always do.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Not because they have to. Because out there somebody's broadcasting, and somebody ought to be listening.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Before you go, take an orange. Take two.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: And next time she drifts, and won't say where, and the heading won't sit still, you'll know. She's bringing you here. For the night.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: The weather, for the Harbour. Calm in the basin. Light airs along the piers.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: A ridge of good sleep moving in from the east. Visibility, as far as the next light.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Outlook for the morning. Departures, as usual. Fair, and kind.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Notices to ships in harbour. Berth three, your aerial is snoring. Berth nine, your operator left a scarf on the bench.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Berth seven, welcome.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: That's the notices. It's a quiet harbour. That's the point of it.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: A moon's gone missing, they say. Well, it's not tied up here. I've checked every berth.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Mind you, if a moon ever needed a night off, there's room at the end of the long pier.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Toast. Every ship in the harbour has woken up at once, sniffing. Thirty old relays, and not a toaster among them.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: I've put some bread on, so nobody's disappointed.

clips.title: The Bit You Hum on the Way Home

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Every ship in the harbour is humming that tune through its vents, and they all stop in the same place.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: I think the ending's the bit you hum on the way home.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Three knocks at the office door. I opened it. I always open it, here. Nobody. Only the lights on the water.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Come in anyway, I said. I've left it on the latch.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: The sky over the harbour has gone a colour I've not seen in all my years here.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: The old ships have tilted their viewports up to look. I haven't seen them so awake in a decade.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: There's a pigeon on the harbour wall. It walked in off the long pier, nodded at me, and asked for berth twelve.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: I didn't argue. It knew the number.

clips.title: The Year Turns at Berth Seven

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: The year turns tonight, at the Harbour, on one hundred and forty point oh. The Nightjar is tied up at berth seven. Leave her there.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Ships don't have to cast off at midnight. Midnight is only a light on the water. If you're going, go on the morning tide. The berth stays yours.

clips.title: The Berth That Isn't Always There

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Leap day, at the Harbour. A day the chart usually skips. We keep a berth for those. Most ships sail straight past it.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: The Nightjar didn't. Tie up, operator. You've an extra day that nobody will log. Spend it with the instruments down. I'll keep the light on.

clips.title: The Longest Light on the Piers

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: Longest light of the year, along the piers. The old relays have their viewports open. They don't see a day this long very often.

lines.speaker: The Harbourmaster
lines.text: The Nightjar can sleep through it. Berth seven, one hundred and forty point oh. I'll keep watch. That's what the long light is for.
